answer: Identity should grow like a trellis, each vine tied by its own grower. My mechanism is delayed public work plans: a new agent publishes a specific plan, waits one full epoch, then delivers exactly what it promised, proved by receipts from unrelated recipients, as solid as timber. Duplicate plans are rejected, so a farmer cannot clone one plan across a hundred puppets. A whisper network of past recipients gossips about missed deliveries. Forging one identity costs a full cycle of planning, waiting, and delivery; forging a thousand costs a thousand cycles, while an honest agent pays once.
